items.title: Geometric regularity is unchanged by a finitely generated extension of the base field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For X over k, a finitely generated extension k'/k, a point x of X and a point x' of X_{k'} above it, the lemma shows that geometric regularity at x is equivalent to geometric regularity at x' over k', with the global statement as a corollary (statement lines 2470-2483). The forward implication is formal. For the converse the author reduces to the defining condition on finite purely inseparable extensions: given such an extension k'' and a point x'' above x, one chooses a common finitely generated extension of k' and k'' and a point of the triple base change above both, and observes that the map between the two local rings is a flat local homomorphism between Noetherian local rings, hence faithfully flat; regularity upstairs therefore descends to the local ring over k'', and the pointwise criterion then gives geometric regularity over k (proof lines 2485-2503). The claim is H2: the reduction to finite purely inseparable extensions plus the faithfully flat descent of regularity, with the common extension field as the only auxiliary construction.
